title: Avoid Sanitary Tees in Horizontal Drain Runs
description: Using a standard sanitary tee to transition from horizontal to horizontal drain piping is a frequent mistake that leads to sluggish flow and recurring clogs. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for horizontal-to-vertical directional changes or vertical stack connections. When installed horizontally, the short radius curve fails to sweep waste smoothly along the flow path, causing solids to drop out and accumulate over time. Instead, use a combination wye and 1/8 bend or a long-sweep elbow for horizontal transitions to maintain proper fluid velocity and smooth waste transport in compliance with standard plumbing codes.

Avoid Sanitary Tees in Horizontal Drain Runs

Using a standard sanitary tee to transition from horizontal to horizontal drain piping is a frequent mistake that leads to sluggish flow and recurring clogs. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for horizontal-to-vertical directional changes or vertical stack connections. When installed horizontally, the short radius curve fails to sweep waste smoothly along the flow path, causing solids to drop out and accumulate over time. Instead, use a combination wye and 1/8 bend or a long-sweep elbow for horizontal transitions to maintain proper fluid velocity and smooth waste transport in compliance with standard plumbing codes.
